title: Sharma's 82 off 32 seals seven-wicket T20 win over Afghanistan
excerpt: Abhishek Sharma smashed 82 off 32 balls to power India's 13.4-over chase at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, taking a 1-0 series lead. Omarzai's 64 lifted Afghanistan to 156/8.
body:
• India chased down 157 in just 13.4 overs at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, winning the first T20I by seven wickets with 38 balls to spare.
  • Abhishek Sharma smashed 82 off 32 balls — seven fours and seven sixes at a strike rate of 256.25 — and was named Player of the Match.
  • Azmatullah Omarzai's 64 off 44 and an 83-run stand with Mohammad Nabi (33) rescued Afghanistan from 41-4 to 156/8.
  • Arshdeep Singh took 3/19 to lead India's bowling; Jasprit Bumrah struck in his first over back after a knee injury, dismissing Rahmanullah Gurbaz for a duck.
  • India lead the three-match series 1-0; the second T20I is on Tuesday, September 15.

India opened their three-match T20I series against Afghanistan with a statement win on Sunday, chasing down a target of 157 in 13.4 overs for a seven-wicket victory at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi. Captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and chose to bowl, and his side never lost control of the match.

The chase was built on one blistering innings. After Sanju Samson fell in the third over, Abhishek Sharma launched a counterattack that took the game away from Afghanistan within minutes. The left-hander smashed 82 off just 32 balls — seven fours and seven sixes at a strike rate of 256.25. He shared a match-winning 121-run partnership off 53 balls for the second wicket with Ishan Kishan, who contributed a measured 42 off 33. Mohammad Nabi struck twice late in the innings to remove both Sharma and Kishan, but Iyer (8 not out off 5) and Tilak Varma (3 not out off 4) guided India over the line against a toothless Rashid Khan, who went wicketless for 34 in 3.4 overs.

Context & Background

This was the first-ever T20I between the two sides hosted in India, and the visitors' innings told the story of a side outclassed by pace and discipline. Jasprit Bumrah, returning after a knee injury, struck with the second ball — dismissing Rahmanullah Gurbaz for a duck with a ball that nipped in and kicked to slip. Afghanistan slipped to 41-4 inside the powerplay, with captain Ibrahim Zadran run out for 11 and Sediqullah Atal (13) and Gulbadin Naib falling soon after.

Azmatullah Omarzai led the recovery with a counter-attacking 64 off 44 balls — four fours and four sixes — carrying Afghanistan past 150. He shared a crucial 83-run partnership off 56 balls with the veteran Mohammad Nabi (33) for the sixth wicket, steadying the innings after a steady stream of wickets. Arshdeep Singh applied the brakes in the death overs, finishing with 3/19 in his four overs, while Varun Chakravarthy removed Darwish Rasooli to make it 43 for 5 in seven overs. India had one familiar problem: with no reliable fifth bowler, Shivam Dube was left to bowl for the first time in the 20th over, and Omarzai took 21 off it.

Impact & Analysis

The 38-ball margin tells its own story. India made a below-par 156/8 look ordinary, and the gap between the sides was widest where it mattered most: Afghanistan's bowling had no answer for Sharma's power. The strike rate of 256.25 was the highest of the night by distance, and his 89 percent control rate — the highest in the match per ESPNcricinfo's tracking — showed this was not slogging but calculated destruction.

For India, the positives stacked up beyond the scoreline. Bumrah's comeback over was lean and hostile, Arshdeep was the pick of the attack, and the chase never touched the middle order. For Afghanistan, Omarzai's all-round value was the standout — 64 with the bat and tight bowling figures of 1/14 — but the top order's collapse and Rashid Khan's wicketless night exposed their ceiling against a top-tier side.

Diaspora Angle

For Indian diaspora fans, this was the kind of evening that reminds you why the T20 format travels so well — the game was decided in under three hours, and Sharma's innings gave overseas supporters a highlight-reel reason to stay up. With the series moving fast and the second T20I just two days away, this is also exactly the kind of series where young Indian talent like Abhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma builds a global following.

What's Next

India face Afghanistan again on Tuesday, September 15, with a chance to seal the series with a game to spare. Afghanistan will need answers for the powerplay — both with bat and ball — after losing four wickets inside six overs and then watching India race past their total in 13.4. For India, the only real question mark is the fifth-bowler quota, which Dube's expensive 20th over underlined. Expect the visitors to shuffle their top order as they chase a series-levelling win.
